prompt: Let $f(x) = x^2 + 1$. The tangent line to the graph at $x = 3$ has slope $f'(3) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(3 + h) - f(3)}{h}$. Find the $y$-intercept of that tangent line.
hint: Two jobs: find the slope with the limit, then write the line through the point $(3, f(3))$.

hints.text: Two jobs: find the slope with the limit, then write the line through the point $(3, f(3))$.

explanation: Point: $f(3) = 9 + 1 = 10$, so the line passes through $(3, 10)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slide down the tangent
steps: Start at $(3, 10)$ on the tangent line. Each step of $1$ to the left drops the height by $6$.
So the tangent crosses the $y$-axis at $-8$.
